```{r setup, include=FALSE}
library(tidyverse)
library(modelr)
library(p8105.datasets)

knitr::opts_chunk$set(
  fig.width = 8,
  fig.asp = 0.65,
  out.width = "90%",
  message = FALSE,
  warning = FALSE
)
theme_set(theme_minimal() + theme(legend.position = "bottom"))
set.seed(2026)
```

## Problem 1: Homicide investigations

```{r homicide-clean}
homicide_df =
  read_csv("data/homicide-data.csv", show_col_types = FALSE) |>
  mutate(
    city_state = str_c(city, state, sep = ", "),
    resolved = as.numeric(disposition == "Closed by arrest"),
    victim_age = as.numeric(victim_age),
    victim_race = factor(victim_race, levels = c("White", "Black")),
    victim_sex = factor(victim_sex, levels = c("Female", "Male"))
  ) |>
  filter(
    !city_state %in% c("Dallas, TX", "Phoenix, AZ", "Kansas City, MO", "Tulsa, AL"),
    victim_race %in% c("White", "Black")
  ) |>
  drop_na(resolved, victim_age, victim_sex, victim_race)

homicide_df |>
  count(city_state, name = "number_of_cases") |>
  knitr::kable()
```

`resolved = 1` denotes cases closed by arrest; `resolved = 0` denotes cases not closed by arrest. 
The comparison of interest is **Male versus Female**, holding victim age and race fixed.

### Baltimore logistic regression

```{r baltimore-model}
baltimore_fit =
  homicide_df |>
  filter(city_state == "Baltimore, MD") |>
  glm(resolved ~ victim_age + victim_sex + victim_race,
      data = _, family = binomial())

broom::tidy(baltimore_fit) |>
  mutate(
    adjusted_or = exp(estimate),
    or_ci_lower = exp(estimate - 1.96 * std.error),
    or_ci_upper = exp(estimate + 1.96 * std.error)
  ) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 3)

baltimore_result =
  broom::tidy(baltimore_fit) |>
  filter(term == "victim_sexMale") |>
  transmute(
    city_state = "Baltimore, MD",
    adjusted_or = exp(estimate),
    lower_ci = exp(estimate - 1.96 * std.error),
    upper_ci = exp(estimate + 1.96 * std.error)
  )

baltimore_result |> knitr::kable(digits = 3)
```

The adjusted odds ratio for case resolution comparing male victims with female victims in Baltimore 
is `r round(baltimore_result$adjusted_or, 3)` (95% CI: `r round(baltimore_result$lower_ci, 3)` to 
`r round(baltimore_result$upper_ci, 3)`). 
An odds ratio less than 1 indicates lower adjusted odds of a case being closed by arrest for male victims; 
an odds ratio greater than 1 indicates higher adjusted odds.

### Fit a model for each city

```{r city-models}
city_or_df =
  homicide_df |>
  nest(city_data = -city_state) |>
  mutate(
    models = map(city_data, \(df) glm(
      resolved ~ victim_age + victim_sex + victim_race,
      data = df, family = binomial()
    )),
    estimates = map(models, broom::tidy)
  ) |>
  select(city_state, estimates) |>
  unnest(estimates) |>
  filter(term == "victim_sexMale") |>
  transmute(
    city_state,
    adjusted_or = exp(estimate),
    lower_ci = exp(estimate - 1.96 * std.error),
    upper_ci = exp(estimate + 1.96 * std.error)
  ) |>
  arrange(adjusted_or)

city_or_df |> knitr::kable(digits = 3)
```

### Plot the adjusted odds ratios

```{r city-plot, fig.height=10}
city_or_df |>
  mutate(city_state = fct_reorder(city_state, adjusted_or)) |>
  ggplot(aes(x = adjusted_or, y = city_state)) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = 1, linetype = "dashed", color = "gray40") +
  geom_errorbar(aes(xmin = lower_ci, xmax = upper_ci), width = 0.2) +
  geom_point(size = 1.7, color = "steelblue4") +
  labs(
    title = "Adjusted odds of homicide resolution: male versus female victims",
    subtitle = "Odds ratios adjusted for victim age and race; 95% Wald confidence intervals",
    x = "Adjusted odds ratio (male vs. female)",
    y = "City"
  )
```

The graph orders cities by their adjusted odds ratios. The dashed vertical line indicates an odds ratio of 1.
Estimates to the left of 1 indicate lower odds of resolution for male victims, while estimates to the right indicate higher odds. 
Confidence intervals crossing 1 do not provide strong evidence of a sex difference at the 5% significance level.

## Problem 2: Bootstrap inference

```{r weather-clean}
data("weather_df")
weather_analysis =
  weather_df |>
  select(tmax, tmin, prcp) |>
  drop_na()

weather_fit = lm(tmax ~ tmin + prcp, data = weather_analysis)

broom::tidy(weather_fit) |> knitr::kable(digits = 3)
broom::glance(weather_fit) |>
  select(r.squared, adj.r.squared, sigma) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 3)
```

The estimated coefficient ratio below is `beta_tmin / beta_prcp`, where both slopes are taken 
from the regression `tmax ~ tmin + prcp`. Their units differ, so the ratio is a mathematical 
summary rather than a dimensionless effect measure.

```{r bootstrap-models}
set.seed(2026)
boot_results =
  weather_analysis |>
  modelr::bootstrap(n = 5000) |>
  mutate(
    models = map(strap, \(df) lm(tmax ~ tmin + prcp, data = df)),
    r_squared = map_dbl(models, \(fit) broom::glance(fit)$r.squared),
    beta_ratio = map_dbl(models, \(fit) {
      betas = coef(fit)
      unname(betas["tmin"] / betas["prcp"])
    })
  ) |>
  select(r_squared, beta_ratio)

boot_results |>
  pivot_longer(everything(), names_to = "quantity", values_to = "estimate") |>
  ggplot(aes(x = estimate)) +
  geom_histogram(bins = 40, fill = "steelblue", color = "white") +
  facet_wrap(~ quantity, scales = "free", ncol = 1) +
  labs(
    title = "Bootstrap distributions from 5,000 resamples",
    x = "Bootstrap estimate", y = "Count"
  )
```

```{r bootstrap-intervals}
boot_summary =
  boot_results |>
  pivot_longer(everything(), names_to = "quantity", values_to = "estimate") |>
  group_by(quantity) |>
  summarize(
    bootstrap_mean = mean(estimate),
    lower_ci = quantile(estimate, 0.025),
    upper_ci = quantile(estimate, 0.975),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

boot_summary |> knitr::kable(digits = 3)
```

Based on 5,000 bootstrap samples, the percentile 95% confidence interval for the regression R-squared 
is [`r round(boot_summary$lower_ci[boot_summary$quantity == "r_squared"], 3)`, 
`r round(boot_summary$upper_ci[boot_summary$quantity == "r_squared"], 3)`]. 
The percentile 95% confidence interval for the ratio of the `tmin` and `prcp` coefficients 
is [`r round(boot_summary$lower_ci[boot_summary$quantity == "beta_ratio"], 3)`, 
`r round(boot_summary$upper_ci[boot_summary$quantity == "beta_ratio"], 3)`]. 
The plots display the sampling variability approximated by bootstrap resampling. 
The ratio may be skewed or unstable if the estimated precipitation coefficient is near zero.
